raw:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which step a student should take to be able to repeat an experiment. The options are A) do the experiment many times, B) keep a record of all procedures, C) make a model of the set-up, or D) change some conditions. 

First, I think about what it means to repeat an experiment. If I want to do the same experiment again, I need to make sure I do everything exactly the same way. Otherwise, the results might not be consistent. So, just doing it many times (Option A) might not be the best approach because if you change something each time, you won't be able to replicate it accurately.

Next, Option B suggests keeping a record of all procedures. That makes sense because if you write down every step you take, you can refer back to it later. This way, you don't forget any details and can ensure each step is the same when you repeat the experiment. It's like having a recipe for a experiment.

Option C is about making a model of the set-up. I'm not entirely sure what that means. Maybe it's creating a diagram or a blueprint of the experiment. That could help visualize the setup, but I'm not sure if it's the first step. It might be useful, but perhaps after you've already recorded the procedures.

Option D is changing some conditions, which doesn't seem right. If you change things, the experiment won't be repeatable. So D is probably incorrect.

Putting it all together, the most logical first step is to keep a record of all procedures. This ensures that each time you do the experiment, you follow the same steps, leading to consistent results. So the answer should be B.
</think>

1. Yes  
2. Reason: The most logical first step to ensure the experiment can be repeated is to keep a record of all procedures. This allows for consistent replication by following the same steps each time, making Option B the correct choice.
